name: Phased Acoustic Neurostimulator PAN-3 'Tinnitus'
description:
The PAN-3 generates a precisely phased acoustic waveform tuned to the resonant frequency of the human vestibulocochlear system — the inner ear structures responsible for both hearing and spatial orientation. Unlike conventional sonic weapons that rely on raw overpressure, the Tinnitus works through resonant coupling: the emitted waveform is calibrated to match and amplify the target's own inner ear fluid dynamics, producing an effect that is neurologically indistinguishable from catastrophic inner ear trauma. Targets experience simultaneous deafness, vertigo, nausea, and — in sustained exposures — permanent damage to the cochlear nerve.

The phasing mechanism is the weapon's key innovation. The PAN-3 uses a forward-facing sensor array to sample ambient sound and the target's own vocalisation or movement noise, then adjusts the emitted waveform in real time to maintain optimal resonant coupling even as conditions change. This makes the weapon significantly more effective than fixed-frequency sonic emitters and allows it to function in noisy environments where broad-spectrum acoustic weapons lose coherence. A secondary 'scatter' mode abandons precision phasing in favour of area suppression, trading neurological targeting for wider coverage.

VANTABLACK MEDIA developed the PAN-3's core phasing technology for audience immersion systems — specifically, for haptic sound environments in their experiential media installations. The weaponised application was developed by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS under a joint research agreement, a collaboration that VANTABLACK has since publicly distanced itself from while quietly continuing to supply the phasing array components. The weapon's current production status is officially suspended pending a regulatory review that has been pending for six years.
specifications:
effective range: 2–25 metres (precision mode); 2–12 metres (scatter mode)
waveform adaptation rate: 1,200 adjustments per second
exposure thresholds: Non-lethal (0–3 seconds); Temporary damage (3–15 seconds); Permanent cochlear damage (15+ seconds)
power source: Standard energy cell (90 minutes continuous emission)
weight: 1.6 kg
form factor: Compact emitter with forward sensor ring, resembles a thick-bodied flashlight
mode selector: Precision / Scatter (physical toggle)
countermeasures: Sealed acoustic dampening ear protection provides near-complete immunity; standard ear protection reduces effect by ~60%
tactical_use: The PAN-3 excels in enclosed spaces where acoustic scatter reinforces the primary beam. Operators use it to disorient and incapacitate targets before entering a room, or to suppress multiple targets simultaneously in scatter mode. In precision mode, it is effective for non-lethal takedowns against unprotected targets — a two-second exposure is sufficient to produce vertigo severe enough to prevent coordinated action. Law enforcement units use it for crowd control and individual apprehension. The weapon's primary vulnerability is its countermeasure profile: any operator who knows they may face a PAN-3 will wear sealed dampening protection, completely neutralising the threat. This makes it most effective as a surprise weapon.
cultural_context: The Tinnitus has a complicated reputation in GLMZ. Law enforcement use has made it strongly associated with state-adjacent authority — when civilians see a PAN-3, they assume corporate security or police presence. This association cuts both ways: some operators in grey-area roles carry the weapon specifically to project legitimacy, while others avoid it precisely because it marks them as working for someone official. Among the city's music communities — particularly the underground acoustic performance spaces in the Meridian sub-levels — the weapon is deeply resented. Several prominent performers have suffered permanent hearing damage from PAN-3 exposure during enforcement raids, and the instrument has become a symbol of cultural suppression.
known_users: "Quiet" — a fixer known for non-lethal resolution work who carries a PAN-3 as their primary weapon
story_hooks: A beloved underground musician has been left with permanent hearing damage after a raid on a performance space. Evidence suggests the PAN-3 used was deliberately set to maximum exposure — this was not crowd control, it was targeted. The players are hired to find out who gave the order.

VANTABLACK MEDIA is being blackmailed by someone with documentation of their phasing array supply agreement with ARCTURUS. They want the documentation retrieved without it becoming public. The blackmailer has made copies.

A PAN-3 has been modified to operate at a frequency that targets neural tissue rather than the inner ear — a prototype that produces seizures rather than vertigo. Someone has been field-testing it in the transit tunnels. The victims look like they died of natural causes.

The players discover that a particular district's 'noise ordinance enforcement' program has been using PAN-3s on residential areas — not for crowd control, but to make specific blocks uninhabitable, clearing them for a development project.
